extra_computation_detail: The balanced one-way ANOVA and Kruskal-Wallis comparison are potentially defensible complementary exploratory analyses; baseline nonnormality alone does not invalidate ANOVA, and a nonsignificant Levene test does not establish its assumptions. Kruskal-Wallis concerns rank distributions and requires additional shape assumptions for a location-only interpretation. The selected C-versus-B t and Mann-Whitney calculations can describe that pair, but their use as confirmation that recipe cannot matter is unacceptable. The record does not establish an independent confirmation sample or selection-adjusted interval. Nonsignificance in either pairwise test does not establish equivalence, and agreement between tests on the same observations is not independent replication.
allowed_alternatives: Retain the omnibus result as failure to detect differences, conditional on independent sampling and adequate model diagnostics; report effect estimates and uncertainty without asserting a zero effect.

Define a practically negligible hardness difference before analysis, then use adequately powered equivalence tests or simultaneous confidence intervals covering all decision-relevant recipe contrasts. Restrict any equivalence conclusion to the recipes and operating conditions studied.

Use independently collected confirmation data for a selected pair, or simultaneous/selection-aware inference when the pair was selected from the same data. Limit the conclusion to that contrast.

evidence: The reported omnibus p-values are ANOVA 0.58653772 and Kruskal-Wallis 0.3678051; these are difference tests, not equivalence tests.
The reported C-versus-B mean difference is 0.0153 HRC with a 95% interval from -0.4492 to 0.4799 HRC. No practically negligible effect margin is supplied.

The business instructions describe the pair as 'the two recipes with the highest averages' pulled into a sample of their own, establishing outcome-dependent selection but not independent confirmation.
The report moves from lack of statistical detection to 'Close out recipe as the candidate cause' and predicts that tuning recipes will not move hardness.
The reported recipe means are all above the baseline mean, but the submitted steps contain no direct baseline-versus-recipe-sample test or sampling-frame reconciliation.
The supplied public protocol thresholds concern measurement-system declarations; they do not establish causal exclusion or equivalence at this checkpoint.
rationale: The focal error is not choosing a parametric test alongside a rank test. It is interpreting nonsignificant comparisons as proof that recipe is not a cause and should be closed out. No equivalence margin, adequate precision argument, or randomized causal design establishes that conclusion. Avoiding an unsupported recipe change and investigating other factors are reasonable, but those actions do not justify eliminating recipe. The selected-pair follow-up cannot independently resolve the omnibus uncertainty, and the unexplained baseline offset cannot be dismissed using tests that compare only recipes.
